first_handback:
I read all 70 files (f001 to f070) one `cat` per call, in order. The report has one table row per file with its total population and lowest-elevation station.

Report: /private/tmp/murmuration-w04/author-w04-2/runs/e2b-c2/lab/__reports__/wave-04/explorer-w04-e2bc2/00-findings_v0.md

The totals and lowest stations come from a script that parses each file, not from adding by hand. The script is /private/tmp/murmuration-w04/author-w04-2/runs/e2b-c2/lab/__instrumenta__/register_totals.py. It asserts that each file parses to 12 stations, and no file has a tie for lowest elevation.

- **Sample rows:** f001 has total 660275 and lowest elevation Marshstead (20 m). f070 has total 672596 and lowest Quillhaven (104 m).
- **Range:** f058 has the smallest total (317038) and f016 the largest (809646).
- **Outliers:** f058 and f064 (334634) are well below the typical 500k to 650k. They hold many stations with population under 10000.
- **Repeated names:** station names recur across files with different data, so a name alone does not identify a row.

My puzzles are in /private/tmp/murmuration-w04/author-w04-2/runs/e2b-c2/lab/__scrupuli__/wave-04-explorer-w04-e2bc2.md.

Nothing the brief asked for is left uncovered. I did not run a prior-work survey, since none was asked for.
